info.title: Getnet Merchant Assistant
info.description: Multi-agent support system: Router, Knowledge, Customer Support, Escalation and Personality.

post.description:
OAuth 2.0 token endpoint (RFC 6749, form encoded). `authorization_code` (PKCE S256) and the rotating
`refresh_token` are the login of the web interface (v0.13.0): both answer
`{access_token, token_type, expires_in, scope, refresh_token}`. `password` (**demonstration only**: smoke test and
CLI, synthetic users) and `client_credentials` (services) answer `{access_token, token_type, expires_in, scope}`.
A failure never says which field was wrong; a refresh token used twice revokes its whole login.

grant_type.description: `authorization_code` (with `code_verifier`, PKCE S256) and `refresh_token` are the login of the web interface. `password` is for the demonstration only (smoke test and CLI). `client_credentials` is for services.

code.description: authorization_code: the code from the redirect.

get.description:
Authorization endpoint (RFC 6749 section 4.1, RFC 7636): shows the issuer's login page. After the login the
browser goes back to `redirect_uri` with a one-use `code` (valid for 60 s), the same `state` and `iss`; the client
exchanges the code at `POST /v1/auth/token` with its `code_verifier`.

schema.description: Exactly one of the client's registered URIs.

post.description:
Revokes the presented token (its `jti`) until it expires (RFC 7009 style: `200` with an empty body). With a
`token` form field holding a refresh token of the same principal, its family (every refresh token of that login
and the access tokens issued with them) is revoked too; any other value is ignored.

token.description: Optional refresh token of the same principal: its whole login is revoked.

post.description:
Continues an `interrupted`, `partial` or `failed` comparison (task 84): cells with a recorded result are not
run again; failed cells, including those with a paid attempt, run again only with `retry_failed=true`. A durable
result of an interrupted cell is restored without a new model call. When every cell already has a result, `202`
with `resumed_cells: 0` closes the comparison. `409 execution_cost_unknown` while the ledger cost of an earlier
execution cannot be read; `409 comparison_running`, `409 comparison_completed`, `409 nothing_to_resume`,
`409 fixed_factors_changed`; `429` budget or demo limit.

get.description:
The token's merchant's conversations, latest activity first (v1.1.0, D2), without message text; the whole
conversation is `GET /v1/conversations/{conversation_id}`. Tokens with no merchant (operator, service) get `403`.
Operator queue, newest first; `state` = open, claimed, answered, rejected or closed.
Summary, pending question, draft, masked conversation, events and deliveries of one case.

post.description: Claims the case for the operator of the token (D9). Claiming one's own case again is idempotent.

`approve`, `reply` or `reject` (D9, D10, D14). The same `idempotency_key` returns the stored record with
`replayed: true`; a case already resumed by another action is `409 already_resumed`.

Sends an exhausted webhook delivery again (spec v0.13.0, D5): the intention behind the attempt `delivery_id`
(listed in `GET /v1/handoffs/{case_id}`, `deliveries`) goes back to `pending` with another round of attempts.
Operator token with `handoff:operate`; audited. `202 {delivery_id, event_id, target, case_id, status: pending,
resend_count}`; `404 delivery_not_found`; `409 delivery_not_exhausted` (pending, delivered or rejected);
`409 delivery_target_not_configured` (the destination has no URL or secret now).

get.description: Public signing keys of the assistant's token issuer (RS256, `kid` = RFC 7638 thumbprint).

get.description:
Prometheus text (0.0.4) from the traces and the budget ledger, cached for 5 s. Public, like `/ready`:
aggregate counts only, no message text, request id, merchant or operator in any label.

post.description:
Sends one merchant message. A bearer access token is required: the merchant comes from the
token's principal, never from the payload (`user_id` is optional and, when present, must match it, otherwise
`403 identity_mismatch`). Operator, service and admin tokens receive `403`.

Two calls: get a token (OAuth 2.0 password grant), then send the message with it.

```bash
TOKEN=$(curl -s localhost:8000/v1/auth/token -d grant_type=password -d username=cliente1988   -d password=cliente1988-fictitious | python -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["access_token"])')
curl -s localhost:8000/messages -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json'   -d '{"message": "When will the money from yesterday sales be deposited?"}'
```

In this page: get the token with `POST /v1/auth/token`, press **Authorize** and paste the `access_token`. The
passwords of `.env.example` are fictitious examples; replace them before exposing the API.

handoff_protocol.description: Protocol of the conversation's handoff case, or null.

pending_operator_reply.title: Pending Operator Reply
pending_operator_reply.description: An attendant's reply is recorded and not yet delivered in a merchant request.

text.title: Text
text.description: Reply text (reply) or instruction to the agent (reject).

message.title: Message
message.description: Merchant message, in Portuguese or English.

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: Optional. The merchant comes from the session; when present it must be the session's merchant (otherwise 403 identity_mismatch). It never selects the merchant.
